module8: Capstone: audit and teach the whole system

The best proof of skill is to check a live system against a plan and then help others use it well. In this capstone you audit a full sales-to-service set-up, fix what you find and train a small group.
Audit in four parts: access, data quality, process stages and service clocks; score each part red, amber or green.
Write a short findings list with the cause, the risk and the fix for each item.
Plan a 30-minute training for one team: one goal, one live demo, one practice task, one feedback question.
Measure the result: compare error counts and user questions before and after the training.
An audit finds 14 percent of open opportunities with no dated next step. The fix is a required field and a weekly report; four weeks later the figure falls to 3 percent.
Audit the practice org with a four-part check list, write the findings, and teach one peer how to fix one finding.
Audit covers all four parts; every finding has a cause and a fix; the peer completes the practice task alone.
quiz: A new support agent needs to see all cases for their region but must not see contract values. Which settings do you use?
Use a profile or permission set for object access, sharing rules for the region, and field settings to hide the contract value field. Give the least access that does the job.
Name the five main objects and say what an opportunity is.
Lead, account, contact, opportunity and case. An opportunity is a possible sale that moves through stages.
A webinar gives 120 sign-ups and 40 match existing contacts. How many new leads should be created, and what should you do first?
Create 80 new leads. First run the duplicate check so the 40 matches are not created again.
Why must every lead have an owner?
Without an owner nobody follows up, so the lead goes cold and reports show false numbers. Every lead needs an owner, a source and a next step.
An opportunity is at stage Quote sent but has no next step. What should the report show and why?
It should flag the record red. A stage must tell the truth about the customer, and no dated next step suggests the sale is stuck.
An important partner is rated B. How many business reviews a year should the plan hold, and what happens to last year's plan?
At least four reviews a year. Last year's plan is closed with an end-period review and then copied forward with new targets.
In the capstone audit you score access, data quality, process stages and service clocks. How do you score each part and what must each finding include?
Score each part red, amber or green. Each finding needs the cause, the risk and the fix.
Gold customers get a 1-hour response. In March 92 of 100 cases met it. What is the result and what next?
The service level was met for 92 percent, so 8 cases were missed. List the missed cases with their causes and fix the common ones.
Why does a case clock pause when the status is waiting for customer?
The delay is not caused by your team, so counting it would be unfair. Pause rules must be written and fair.
You want to add a new required field. Describe a safe release and the final check.
Test in a sandbox with a few users, release with a one-page note and a rollback plan, then check for errors the next working day.
ladder: L1 Basic
Remember the main CRM words: lead, account, contact, opportunity and case. Find each one on screen without changing any data.
Ask learners to point to each object and say it in their own words. Common mistake: mixing up a lead and a contact.
L2 Awareness
Understand why access rules exist and how the three layers of profile, sharing and fields protect customers. Explain in simple words why least access is safer.
Use the support agent example. Check that learners can say what each layer controls. Common mistake: giving everyone full access to save time.
L3 Foundation
Apply the lead life cycle by creating a campaign, routing leads and converting the qualified ones. Close the rest with a reason.
Watch for duplicate accounts and leads without an owner. Let the learner drive the screen. Common mistake: skipping the duplicate check.
L4 Practitioner
Apply a stage path with exit proof, dated next steps, quotes and forecast categories. Keep each record honest to the customer's real position.
Review two opportunities together and ask what proof supports each stage. Common mistake: moving a stage on hope, not proof.
L5 Specialist
Analyse accounts and partners to segment them, write plans and set a review calendar. Compare a good visit report with a weak one.
Ask for numbers in every goal and a date on every action. Common mistake: plans that are written once and never reviewed.
L6 Advanced
Evaluate service performance using queues, clocks and four service numbers. Judge whether the targets are fair and what causes missed cases.
Have learners read a dashboard and name the biggest cause of misses. Common mistake: trusting one average and ignoring the late cases.
L7 Super expert
Create a governance pack and audit a whole system, then teach others to use it. Show that data, change, people and audit rules each have an owner.
Check that every rule has an owner, a test and a date. Common mistake: governance so heavy that people work around it.
